newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Van Miert warns Major over BA-American deal.
newsitem.headline: EU's Van Miert warns Major over BA-American deal.

text.p: The EU's top competition official reacted firmly to British Prime Minister John Major's comments that the review of the alliance between British Airways and American Airlines is a matter for the British authorities.

"Unless the British decision would completely satisfy also our competition concerns...there will be a major problem," European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert told Reuters Television on Thursday evening.
"If that is not the case, then we will have to take the member state to court for ignoring Community law and Community obligations" he said.

Major told the House of Commons earlier on Thursday that Britain's Director General of Fair Trading would consider the Commission's views on the link-up between British Airways and AMR's American Airlines when preparing advice for President of the Board of Trade Ian Lang.
He added: "But it will be for Mr Lang to decide whether to clear the alliance."

Britain and the Commission have been on a collision course over the transatlantic alliance since the British Office of Fair Trading announced in early December it would clear the deal provided the two airlines agreed to give away 168 weekly takeoff and landing slots at the congested London-Heathrow airport.
BA indicated that it would agree to surrender the slots if it could sell them.
But both Van Miert and European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock have said that slots can only be exchanged or given away, not sold, under EU civil aviation rules.
Van Miert did not contest the British authorities' own right to vet the alliance, but said its assessment and that of the Commission could not differ.
Asked why the British government was apparently unwilling to cooperate with the Commission on the case, he admitted that the upcoming general elections may play a role:
"You should ask the British government, but since there are elections in the air, who knows," he told RTV in an interview
The alliance is also being examined by U.S. authorities.

The Commission said earlier on Thursday that the deal would completely eliminate competition on 14 routes between Britain and the United States, including London-Dallas, Birmingham-New-York and Glasgow-Boston.
